$comment: The RAM -> model ladder, largest first, so 'the first that fits' and 'the largest
that fits' are the same walk. Ordering is asserted by the test suite against
min_ram_gb; an entry inserted in the wrong place fails there rather than quietly
returning a smaller model than the machine could have run.
This file is DATA. No code lives here, so a non-Python host can read it directly.
Weights are the floor, not the total: KV cache, activations and the runtime's
arena sit on top. These fractions are rough figures and should be described as
such wherever they are shown to a user.
0.7 because a desktop has swap and no low-memory killer, and because the
default GPU wired limit on a large macOS machine is around 0.75 of total.
The 1 GiB overhead floor is sized for a 32k KV cache. Lower usable_fraction
if the machine runs other large processes.
Stricter than desktop: a mobile low-memory killer takes the process rather
than swapping, so the headroom has to be real.
The text-only build, deliberately. A vision-fused variant of the same language
model can be more than twice the size, and some fused builds are packaged for
a different runtime and will not load in llama.cpp at all.
The floor rung: whatever the target was built with. An embedded image supplies
its own GGUF, so there is no download and no network requirement.
